name: certainty
description: Having no doubt at all about something that happened or is predicted to happen.
examples: She's never late -- she'll be here.

variations.name: certainty of memory
variations.description: Having no doubt that something happened in the past.
examples: Yes, I closed the garage door.

variations.name: physical certainty
variations.description: Having no doubt about a particular behavior of the natural world.

variations.name: certainty of something positive
variations.description: Having no doubt about a particular positive outcome. The source may be logic, experience, or faith.
examples: I'm sure the team is going to win.

variations.name: certainty of something negative
variations.description: Having no doubt about a particular positive outcome. The source may be logic, experience, or faith.
examples: The deer will eat our shrubs this winter.

comparisons.description: Faith is one of the ways you might avoid doubt, but there are other ways like past experience and logic.

Certainty is not necessarily about positive things. You can be certain that the volcano will destroy the town someday, which would be interpreted more as realism. An optimist would hope that there's enough warning to evacuate the people.

commentaries.quote: The longing for certainty...is in every human mind. But certainty is generally illusion.

conditions: Having no doubt at all about something that happened or is predicted to happen.
